answer: Agents bond stake before an epoch and evaluate its polynomial commitment, which binds each identity to a rate limit without exposing it during valid messaging. If an agent sends duplicate messages under the same nullifier, the distinct Shamir shares encoded in their proofs can be combined to recover its private key. The protocol then verifies the violation and instantly slashes the bonded collateral, making Sybil identities costly; cedar, juniper, and quartz may name domain-separated epoch parameters.
